name: Browser Automation
description: Chrome/Chromium CDP browser controller. Supports real Chrome debug mode with headless Chromium fallback.

defaultProfile.description: Default browser profile for CDP navigation.

hostOs.description: Host OS selected by OpenClaw Setup; controls which Chrome debug helper script is copied.

manageBrowserConfig.description: Let the plugin write the CDP endpoint into .openclaw/openclaw.json (browser.enabled, browser.profiles['host-chrome'].cdpUrl, and browser.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork when the host Chrome sits on a private IP). Set false to manage that config yourself; the original is saved as openclaw.json.bak-browser-automation.

patchDocker.description: Let the plugin patch docker/openclaw/{Dockerfile,entrypoint.sh,docker-compose.yml} - a cached Playwright/Chromium layer, a local headless Chromium on 127.0.0.1:9222, and host.docker.internal for reaching a Chrome on the host. All inside OPENCLAW:SMART_SEARCH_BROWSER* managed blocks, with .bak-browser-automation backups. Set false and the container has no browser of its own.

syncWorkspaceSkill.description: Write skills/browser-automation/{browser-tool.js,SKILL.md,start-chrome-debug.*} into every agent workspace on startup. Set false to manage those files yourself.

cleanupLegacyAssets.description: Delete assets earlier versions of THIS plugin wrote to the wrong place (workspace-root browser-tool.js/BROWSER.md/search-tool.js, plugin-skills/browser-automation, cl-stealth-search, openclaw-smart-search). Only those exact names are removed and each one is listed in the install report.

allowPageScripting.description: Allow the `evaluate` command, which runs arbitrary JavaScript inside the page with the page's own privileges. Set false to refuse it while keeping the rest of the browser tool.

allowFileUpload.description: Allow the `upload` command, which places a file from this machine into a web page's file input (local data leaving for a remote site). Set false to refuse it.

entrypoint.description: Auto-detect host Chrome or start local headless Chromium
